### Setup project and run tests

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-plugin-yaml/README.md

Install dependencies and execute the test suite when contributing to the plugin.

```bash
$ bun install # project setup
$ bun test # run tests
```

--------------------------------

### Install and run global packages

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

Use the -g or --global flag with bun install to install command-line tools globally, followed by example output when running the installed tool.

```bash
bun install --global cowsay # or `bun install -g cowsay`
cowsay "Bun!"
```

```txt
 ______
< Bun! >
 ------
        \   ^__^
         \  (oo)\_______
            (__)\       )/\
                ||----w |
                ||     ||
```

--------------------------------

### Configure local template setup logic in `package.json`

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/templating/create.mdx

Defines `preinstall`, `postinstall`, and `start` scripts in the `bun-create` section of a local template's `package.json`.

```json
{
  "name": "@bun-examples/simplereact",
  "version": "0.0.1",
  "main": "index.js",
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^17.0.2",
    "react-dom": "^17.0.2"
  },
  "bun-create": {
    "preinstall": "echo 'Installing...'", // a single command
    "postinstall": ["echo 'Done!'"], // an array of commands
    "start": "bun run echo 'Hello world!'"
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Valid shortened import paths example setup

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/import/no-useless-path-segments.mdx

Demonstrates valid, simplified relative import paths in src/pages/home.js that are not reported.

```js
export function formatDate() {}
```

```js
export function Header() {}
```

```js
import { formatDate } from "../format.js";
import { Header } from "./header.js";
```

### Install project dependencies

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/remix.mdx

Navigate into the project directory and install dependencies with bun install.

```sh
cd my-remix-app
bun install
```

--------------------------------

### Install project dependencies

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/solidstart.mdx

Navigate into the newly created project directory and install dependencies with Bun.

```sh
cd my-app
bun install
```

--------------------------------

### Install Bun in GitHub Actions with setup-bun

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/install/cicd.mdx

Use the official oven-sh/setup-bun action in a GitHub Actions runner step to install Bun and execute commands like bun install.

```yaml
name: my-workflow
jobs:
  my-job:
    name: my-job
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # ...
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 # [!code ++]

      # run any `bun` or `bunx` command
      - run: bun install # [!code ++]
```

### Start development server with bun dev

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/src/runtime/cli/init/README2.default.md

Starts the local development server for the project.

```bash
bun dev
```

--------------------------------

### Install a package using bun install

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/snippets/cli/install.mdx

Install a package by specifying its package name and target version.

```sh
bun install <name>@<version>
```

--------------------------------

### Start the HTTP server using bun run

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/quickstart.mdx

Start the server locally and view the listening address.

```bash
bun run index.ts
```

```txt
Listening on http://localhost:3000/
```

--------------------------------

### Install all project dependencies with bun install

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

Installs dependencies, devDependencies, and optionalDependencies for a project, runs lifecycle scripts, and writes a bun.lock file.

```bash
bun install
```

--------------------------------

### Set the installation strategy using the --linker flag

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/isolated-installs.mdx

Pass `--linker isolated` or `--linker hoisted` to `bun install` to choose between strict dependency isolation and traditional flattened installs.

```bash
# Use isolated installs
bun install --linker isolated

# Use traditional hoisted installs
bun install --linker hoisted
```

--------------------------------

### Install Dependencies with Hardlink Backend

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

Force the hardlink backend during installation. This is the default backend on Linux and Windows.

```bash
rm -rf node_modules
bun install --backend hardlink
```

--------------------------------

### Disallowed hook usage in test setup

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/vitest/no-hooks.mdx

An example of test setup using `beforeEach` that triggers a lint rule report.

```ts
import { beforeEach, expect, test } from "vitest";

let cart;

beforeEach(() => {
  cart = createCart();
});

test("starts empty", () => {
  expect(cart.items).toEqual([]);
});
```

--------------------------------

### Set up toolchains and run homepage benchmarks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/bench/site/README.md

Sets up required toolchains and repositories, then executes the benchmark suite using a specified Bun binary under test. Supports running full suites, specific sub-benchmarks, or quick smoke tests via environment variables.

```sh
bench/site/setup-toolchains.sh                      # node, deno, pnpm/yarn/npm, bun release + canary -> $SITEBENCH_HOME/toolchains
bench/site/setup-repos.sh                           # rolldown/benchmarks clone + deps of bench/express, bench/websocket-server, bench/postgres
BUN=/abs/path/to/bun bench/site/run-all.sh          # everything: bundler http ws postgres install (~30 min with RUNS=3)
BUN=/abs/path/to/bun bench/site/run-all.sh http ws  # a subset
RUNS=1 BUN=... bench/site/run-all.sh                # quick smoke run
```

Install the benchmark dependencies using Bun package manager.

```bash
bun install

### Correct test title starting with lowercase letter

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/jest/prefer-lowercase-title.mdx

An example of a test title starting with a lowercase letter, which complies with the rule.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "@jest/globals";

test("adds an item", () => {
  expect(cart.add(item)).toBe(1);
});
```

--------------------------------

### Incorrect test title starting with uppercase letter

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/jest/prefer-lowercase-title.mdx

An example of a test title starting with an uppercase letter, which is reported by the rule.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "@jest/globals";

test("Adds an item", () => {
  expect(cart.add(item)).toBe(1);
});
```

### Initialize project and install @neondatabase/serverless

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/neon-serverless-postgres.mdx

Creates a new project directory, initializes a Bun project with defaults, and adds Neon's serverless driver dependency.

```sh
mkdir bun-neon-postgres
cd bun-neon-postgres
bun init -y
bun add @neondatabase/serverless
```

--------------------------------

### Valid test setup inside hooks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/require-hook.mdx

Example of compliant test structure with setup logic placed inside `beforeAll` and `beforeEach` hooks.

```ts
import { beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, mock, setDefaultTimeout, test } from "bun:test";

setDefaultTimeout(10_000);
mock.module("./mailer", () => ({ send: mock() }));

const names = ["ada", "grace"];
let db;

beforeAll(() => {
  db = connect();
  db.seed(names);
});

describe("users", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    clearCache();
  });

  test("finds a user", () => {
    expect(db.find("ada")).toBeDefined();
  });
});
```

--------------------------------

### Initialize project and install Drizzle and Neon dependencies

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/neon-drizzle.mdx

Create a new project directory, initialize it with Bun, and install drizzle-orm, the Neon serverless driver, and drizzle-kit.

```sh
mkdir bun-drizzle-neon
cd bun-drizzle-neon
bun init -y
bun add drizzle-orm @neondatabase/serverless
bun add -D drizzle-kit
```

### False positive example when combining flags

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/oxc/bad-bitwise-operator.mdx

Example pattern where bitwise flag combining gets reported because the right-hand operand is a property access.

```js
const mode = flags | Mode.Write;

```

--------------------------------

### Explicit setup within test without hooks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/vitest/no-hooks.mdx

An example of self-contained test setup that avoids shared hook state and passes the lint rule.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

test("starts empty", () => {
  const cart = createCart();
  expect(cart.items).toEqual([]);
});
```

### Initialize Prisma with SQLite datasource provider

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/prisma.mdx

Uses bunx to run prisma init, generating the schema file, migration directory, and writing DATABASE_URL to .env.

```bash
bunx --bun prisma init --datasource-provider sqlite
```

--------------------------------

### Add start script to package.json

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/quickstart.mdx

Configure a start script in package.json to run the TypeScript entrypoint with Bun.

```json
{
  "name": "my-app",
  "module": "index.ts",
  "type": "module",
  "private": true,
  "scripts": { // [!code ++]
    "start": "bun run index.ts" // [!code ++]
  }, // [!code ++]
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/bun": "latest"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "typescript": "^7"
  }
}
```

### Valid comments example

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/eslint/capitalized-comments.mdx

Demonstrates allowed comments: starting with an uppercase letter, starting with a number, containing a URL, or matching tool directives like eslint-disable.

```js
// Retry once, then give up
await send(message);

// 3 attempts at most
// https://example.com/retries explains why
/* eslint-disable-next-line no-console */
console.log("sent");
```

### Autolink URLs with fragments

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/bun/md/spec-permissive-autolinks.txt

Parses optional URL fragments starting with '#' appended to the domain or path.

```example
https://example.com#fragment
.
<p><a href="https://example.com#fragment">https://example.com#fragment</a></p>
.
--fpermissive-url-autolinks
```

### Valid interface with grouped overloads

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/typescript/adjacent-overload-signatures.mdx

Example not reported by the rule because all overload signatures for get are grouped consecutively.

```ts
interface Storage {
  get(key: string): string;
  get(key: string, fallback: string): string;
  clear(): void;
}
```

--------------------------------

### Correct usage with slice()

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/unicorn/prefer-string-slice.mdx

Example of compliant string slicing using `slice()` specifying the start and end positions.

```js
const year = date.slice(0, 4);
const month = date.slice(5, 7); // 7 is the end
```

--------------------------------

### Global test setup with beforeAll and afterAll hooks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/test/configuration.mdx

Define database setup and teardown handlers using `bun:test` hooks in a preload script.

```typescript
// Global test setup
import { beforeAll, afterAll } from "bun:test";

beforeAll(() => {
  // Set up test database
  setupTestDatabase();
});

afterAll(() => {
  // Clean up
  cleanupTestDatabase();
});
```

### Reported warning comments example

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/eslint/no-warning-comments.mdx

Shows invalid comments that trigger the default `no-warning-comments` rule at the start of a comment.

```js
// TODO: handle an empty list
function total(items) {
  /* fixme: rounding */
  return items.length * 1.1;
}
```

Example of regular expression syntax reported by `no-div-regex` due to ambiguity with `/=`.

```js
const value = line.replace(/=\s*/, "");
```

### Reported usage of beforeEach hook

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/jest/no-hooks.mdx

Example of test setup using `beforeEach` that triggers the `jest/no-hooks` lint rule violation.

```ts
import { beforeEach, expect, test } from "@jest/globals";

let cart;

beforeEach(() => {
  cart = createCart();
});

test("starts empty", () => {
  expect(cart.items).toEqual([]);
});
```

export function Header() {}

### Valid comments example

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/eslint/no-warning-comments.mdx

Shows valid comments that do not trigger the rule because warning terms are not matching whole words at the start.

```js
// An empty list gives 0.
function total(items) {
  // Todos are counted like any other item.
  return items.length * 1.1;
}
```

### Examples of bun info queries

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/info.mdx

Illustrates common `bun info` commands including querying package information, versions, dependencies, homepages, and JSON output.

```bash
# View basic package information
bun info is-number

# View a specific version
bun info is-number@7.0.0

# View all available versions
bun info is-number versions

# View package dependencies
bun info express dependencies

# View package homepage
bun info lodash homepage

# Get JSON output
bun info react --json
```

import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

writeFileSync("/tmp/report.json", JSON.stringify(report));
writeFileSync(`/var/tmp/${name}.log`, lines.join("\n"));
```

### Incorrect usage without braces

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/eslint/curly.mdx

Examples of single-line if statements and loops without braces that get reported under default configuration.

```js
if (!user) redirect("/login");

for (const item of items) total += item.price;
```

--------------------------------

### Avoid reporting by not exporting unimported functions

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/import/no-unused-modules.mdx

Example setup where `formatTime` in `shop/format.js` is not exported, avoiding lint warnings for unused exports.

```json
{
  "root": true,
  "plugins": ["import"],
  "parserOptions": { "ecmaVersion": "latest", "sourceType": "module" },
  "rules": { "import/no-unused-modules": ["error", { "unusedExports": true }] }
}
```

```js
import { formatDate } from "./format.js";

console.log(formatDate(new Date()));
```

```js
export function formatDate(date) {}
function formatTime(date) {}
```

### Start the SvelteKit production server

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/sveltekit.mdx

Start the built application server with Bun. The server listens on port 3000 by default unless configured using the `PORT` environment variable.

```txt
Listening on http://0.0.0.0:3000/
```

--------------------------------

### Restricted modifier example (reported)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/no-restricted-matchers.mdx

Demonstrates that restricting a modifier such as `{ resolves = "" }` causes all chains starting with `resolves` to be reported.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

test("loads the user", async () => {
  await expect(loadUser(1)).resolves.toEqual({ id: 1 });
  await expect(loadUser(2)).resolves.not.toBeNull();
});
```

### Report unused exports across multiple files

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/import/no-unused-modules.mdx

Example setup reporting an unused export because `formatTime` is exported from `shop/format.js` but never imported by `shop/app.js`.

```json
{
  "root": true,
  "plugins": ["import"],
  "parserOptions": { "ecmaVersion": "latest", "sourceType": "module" },
  "rules": { "import/no-unused-modules": ["error", { "unusedExports": true }] }
}
```

```js
import { formatDate } from "./format.js";

console.log(formatDate(new Date()));
```

```js
export function formatDate(date) {}
export function formatTime(date) {}
```

--------------------------------

### Worker postMessage false positive example

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/unicorn/require-post-message-target-origin.mdx

Demonstrates worker postMessage calls that get reported because the rule cannot distinguish worker instances from window instances.

```js
const worker = new Worker("./resize.js");
worker.postMessage(image);

```

--------------------------------

### build.onStart

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/plugins.mdx

Registers a callback that runs when the bundler starts a new bundle. The bundler waits for all onStart callbacks to complete before continuing.

```APIDOC
### build.onStart(callback)

Registers a callback that runs when the bundler starts a new bundle.

#### Parameters
- **callback** (`() => void | Promise<void>`) - Required - The function to execute at the start of bundling. Can return a Promise.

#### Return Value
- `void`

#### Example
```ts
build.onStart(async () => {
  console.log("Bundle started!");
});
```
```

--------------------------------

### Start a simple HTTP server with Bun.serve

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/http/simple.mdx

Starts an HTTP server listening on port 3000 that responds to every request with status 200 and "Welcome to Bun!".

```typescript
const server = Bun.serve({
  port: 3000,
  fetch(request) {
    return new Response("Welcome to Bun!");
  },
});

console.log(`Listening on ${server.url}`);
```

### Configure security scanner in bunfig.toml

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/security-scanner-api.mdx

Configures Bun to scan packages before installation. Replace the example package name with your scanner's actual package name.

```toml
[install.security]
scanner = "@oven/bun-security-scanner" # example name, replace with your scanner's package
```

### Escape block quote marker for literal setext heading

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/bun/md/spec.txt

Use backslash escapes when literal text starting with a block quote marker is intended as a setext heading.

```example
\> foo
------
.
<h2>&gt; foo</h2>
```

--------------------------------

### Autolink URLs with paths

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/bun/md/spec-permissive-autolinks.txt

Matches optional URL paths starting with '/' and delimited by slashes. Non-alphanumerical characters (., -, _) in path components must be bounded by alphanumerical characters.

```example
https://example.com/images/branding/logo_272x92.png
.
<p><a href="https://example.com/images/branding/logo_272x92.png">https://example.com/images/branding/logo_272x92.png</a></p>
.
--fpermissive-url-autolinks
```

### Configure bunfig.toml and run Fullstack Dev Server

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-plugin-svelte/README.md

Register bun-plugin-svelte under serve.static plugins in bunfig.toml, then run the dev server with an HTML entrypoint.

```toml

plugins = ["bun-plugin-svelte"]

```

```sh
$ bun index.html

```

--------------------------------

### Valid single and nested hooks example

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/no-duplicate-hooks.mdx

Demonstrates valid hook usage by combining setup actions into a single `beforeEach` per block or isolating them into nested `describe` blocks.

```ts
import { beforeEach, describe, test } from "bun:test";

describe("cart", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cart.clear();
    cart.add("apple");
  });

  test("has one item", () => {});

  describe("after checkout", () => {
    beforeEach(() => {
      cart.checkout();
    });

    test("is empty", () => {});
  });
});

```

### Start an HTTP server with Bun.serve

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/bun-apis.mdx

Starts an HTTP server using `Bun.serve` with standard `Request` and `Response` objects in server.ts.

```ts
Bun.serve({
  fetch(req: Request) {
    return new Response("Success!");
  },
});
```

--------------------------------

### Get current file name with import.meta.file

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/util/import-meta-file.mdx

Use `import.meta.file` to retrieve the filename of the currently executing module (for example, evaluating inside `/a/b/c.ts` returns `"c.ts"`).

```ts
import.meta.file; // => "c.ts"
```

--------------------------------

### Incorrect test blocks without padding (Reported)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/vitest/padding-around-test-blocks.mdx

Shows an example where test calls directly follow setup code and each other without separating blank lines, causing a lint violation.

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

describe("cart", () => {
  const cart = createCart();
  test("starts empty", () => {
    expect(cart.items).toEqual([]);
  });
  test.skip("adds an item", () => {
    expect(cart.add("apple").items).toEqual(["apple"]);
  });
});
```

### Run initial Prisma database migration

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/prisma-postgres.mdx

Creates and applies the initial SQL migration to the PostgreSQL database. Pass --env-file=.env because Bun does not load .env automatically when executing CLIs with --bun.

```bash
bun run --bun --env-file=.env prisma migrate dev --name init
```

```txt
Loaded Prisma config from prisma.config.ts.

Prisma schema loaded from prisma/schema.prisma.
Datasource "db": PostgreSQL database "mydb", schema "public" at "localhost:5432"

Applying migration `20250114141233_init`

The following migration(s) have been created and applied from new schema changes:

prisma/migrations/
  └─ 20250114141233_init/
    └─ migration.sql

Your database is now in sync with your schema.
```

--------------------------------

### Invalid test code violating require-hook

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/require-hook.mdx

Example of invalid test setup where initialized `let` variables and standalone function calls are placed outside hooks at the top level or directly in a `describe` block.

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";

let db = connect();
db.seed(["ada", "grace"]);

describe("users", () => {
  clearCache();

  test("finds a user", () => {
    expect(db.find("ada")).toBeDefined();
  });
});
```

### Define an HTTP route and start an Elysia server in server.ts

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/elysia.mdx

Define a GET route at root using Elysia and listen on port 8080. Logs the running server port using the app.server instance.

```ts
import { Elysia } from "elysia";

const app = new Elysia().get("/", () => "Hello Elysia").listen(8080);

console.log(`🦊 Elysia is running on port ${app.server?.port}...`);
```

## PluginBuilder.onStart()

### Run shell commands with Bun Shell quickstart

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/shell.mdx

Execute shell commands using the $ template tag and pass JavaScript objects like fetch Response instances directly into stdin.

```ts
import { $ } from "bun";

const response = await fetch("https://example.com");

// Use Response as stdin.
await $`cat < ${response} | wc -c`; // 1256
```

### Create a local template directory and `package.json`

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/templating/create.mdx

Creates a template folder inside `$HOME/.bun-create` and defines a minimal `package.json` for it.

```bash
cd $HOME/.bun-create
mkdir foo
cd foo
```

```json
{
  "name": "foo"
}
```

### Serve frontend with Bun.serve and HTML imports

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/src/runtime/cli/init/rule.md

Demonstrates setting up a full-stack server using Bun.serve with route handlers, WebSockets, HTML imports, and React/CSS bundling. Run index.ts using bun --hot for hot reloading.

```ts
import index from "./index.html"

Bun.serve({
  routes: {
    "/": index,
    "/api/users/:id": {
      GET: (req) => {
        return new Response(JSON.stringify({ id: req.params.id }));
      },
    },
  },
  // optional websocket support
  websocket: {
    open: (ws) => {
      ws.send("Hello, world!");
    },
    message: (ws, message) => {
      ws.send(message);
    },
    close: (ws) => {
      // handle close
    }
  },
  development: {
    hmr: true,
    console: true,
  }
})
```

```html
<html>
  <body>
    <h1>Hello, world!</h1>
    <script type="module" src="./frontend.tsx"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

```tsx
import React from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";

// import .css files directly and it works
import './index.css';

const root = createRoot(document.body);

export default function Frontend() {
  return <h1>Hello, world!</h1>;
}

root.render(<Frontend />);
```

```sh
bun --hot ./index.ts
```

```

--------------------------------

### Common bunx execution examples

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/snippets/cli/bunx.mdx

Demonstrates executing binaries for Prisma and Prettier, targeting specific package versions, mapping differing binary names with -p, and enforcing Bun runtime execution with --bun.

```bash
# Run Prisma migrations
bunx prisma migrate

# Format a file with Prettier
bunx prettier foo.js

# Run a specific version of a package
bunx uglify-js@3.14.0 app.js

# Use --package when binary name differs from package name
bunx -p @angular/cli ng new my-app

# Force running with Bun instead of Node.js, even if the executable contains a Node shebang
bunx --bun vite dev foo.js
```

### Example project structure for concurrent and sequential test files

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/test/concurrent-test-glob.mdx

Shows an example directory layout organizing sequential unit tests and concurrent integration test files.

```sh
my-project/
├── bunfig.toml
├── tests/
│   ├── unit/
│   │   ├── math.test.ts          # Sequential
│   │   └── utils.test.ts         # Sequential
│   └── integration/
│       ├── concurrent-api.test.ts     # Concurrent
│       └── concurrent-database.test.ts # Concurrent
```

### Valid setup code inside lifecycle hooks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/vitest/require-hook.mdx

Complies with the rule by placing top-level setup inside `beforeAll` and `describe`-level setup inside `beforeEach`.

```javascript
import { beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";

vi.mock("./mailer");

const names = ["ada", "grace"];
let db;

beforeAll(() => {
  db = connect();
  db.seed(names);
});

describe("users", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    clearCache();
  });

  test("finds a user", () => {
    expect(db.find("ada")).toBeDefined();
  });
});
```
